newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Export growth separates best from rest in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Export growth separates best from rest in Hungary.

text.p: Fast growth in exports to the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) made Hungary's Richter and Graboplast investors' favourites after the first-half earnings season, analysts said on Tuesday.
Chemicals group TVK and OTP Bank also joined the group of best performers, while retailer Fotex reinforced hopes that a consumer recovery is finally materialising in Hungary.
The rest of the market released a mixed batch of earnings, triggering a wide range of analyst recommendations.

"Richter's(pharmaceuticals)sales in Russia were strong, its margins were strong, too, and its revenue shifted towards finished products," said Gabor Sitanyi, analyst at ING Barings in London. "These factors did not come as a surprise, though, as we saw them already in the first quarter."

Richter's operating margin grew to 31.2 percent in the first half of 1997 from 28.9 percent as it benefited from a strong dollar. The company exports about two-thirds of its products and most of those sales are invoiced in dollars, while its operating expenses incur mainly in forint.
Its exports rose $14.6 million or 17.5 percent to $98 million, primarily on a strong demand from the CIS countries.

Merrill Lynch on Monday kept its "buy" rating for Richter, despite downgrading the Hungarian market as a whole from overweight to neutral because of the bourse's vulnerability to swings in international investor sentiment and its less attractive valuation.

First-half figures also put home improvement product maker Graboplast among analysts' top picks. Bank Austria Investment upgraded it to 'buy' from 'accumulate', while Merrill Lynch said it saw upside potential for domestic-oriented companies, including Graboplast.
The only blemish that analysts found around Graboplast was the risk of dilution, as the company once again planned to raise its share capital to finance expansion.
"Graboplast's results were above expectations," said Rudi Voros, analyst at ICE Securities in London.

"The only negative thing with Graboplast is that it wants to raise its capital again," he said. "However, one has to add that investors have been compensated for the dilution effect that stems from the capital increase by very good earnings."
Graboplast, which regards acquisitions and expansions key to its success, said earnings per share jumped to 259 forints in the first half of 1997 from 129 forints in the same period of 1996.
Graboplast's first-half consolidated operating profits rose to 1.062 billion forints from 719.9 million, and after-tax profit grew to 1.097 billion forints from 423.1 million.

The Graboplast group also benefited from the CIS markets. Its total east European sales amounted to $15.1 million, with sales to CIS countries reaching $8.9 million, up 53 percent over the same period of last year.
TVK benefited from world market prices of naptha but analysts expected the company's fortunes to change in the fourth quarter with prices in ethylene seen declining due to higher global supply.

OTP Bank, like any other banks in Hungary, felt the impact of narrowing interest margins but is expected to keep its margin above the market's average, analysts said. As Hungary's largest commercial bank it has a good access to relatively low-interest retail deposits.
OTP said at the end of June it handled 61 percent of the population's retail forint deposits and 47 percent of the retail hard currency deposits.
